findings.biggest_remaining_problem: The model is not segmenting cracks at all - it is segmenting "high local texture variance," and the wedge suppression is now a hard axis-aligned box that deletes the single best crack in the frame. Quantitatively: red = 28.6% of the frame and 80% of that mass is ONE connected amorphous blob (63,422 of 78,900 px, ~23% of frame). Mean panel-1 intensity inside red (136.6) is indistinguishable from outside (140.3), while local std inside red is ~2x outside (30.6 vs 16.0) - proof the classifier keys on deformation mottling / relief texture, not on dark thin linear voids. The mask boundary meanders through texture and never traces a line; it is blobby, isotropic, and 19% of it sits on genuinely bland matrix (local sd below the frame median). Simultaneously the suppression over-fires: the four largest near-black elongated features - x277-377/y306-325 (the 100-px central dark crack trace), x383-437/y301-320, x594-619/y206-224, x541-592/y220-232 - have EXACTLY 0.000 red coverage. A straight vertical mask edge at column 598 spanning 147 rows, plus straight horizontal edges around the central dark trace, confirms rectangular box suppression rather than a learned decision. The most unambiguous crack in the image is at native x~500-620, y~190-250: a classic open crack with a dark void core and bright phase-contrast fringes, propagating LEFT from the mid-dark uniform wedge/notch that intrudes at the right frame edge, tapering to a crack tip, with 2-3 converging branches. That is textbook crack-from-notch-tip and it sits in a clean rectangular hole in the mask surrounded by a sea of red on featureless matrix. So the wedge rim itself is no longer being traced (suppression works on the wedge), but the box swallowed the crack emanating from the wedge tip - the exact structure the specimen owner cares about. Only incidental fragments of the crack network get red (x467-500/y203-221, x537-585/y193-201, x423-462/y350-362, x245-271/y307-316 are covered, but only because the giant blob happens to sweep over them, not because they were traced). Net effect: precision and recall fail at the same time, and the suppression is now actively harmful. Fix direction: replace area-thresholded texture/variance response with an anisotropy-gated ridge/valley detector (require elongation and dark-core polarity), and replace the rectangular wedge box with a tight morphological mask of the wedge body only, dilated by a few px, so cracks emanating from the notch tip survive.

The mask is anti-localised with respect to the cracks: it blanket-fills the deformed high-relief material AROUND the damage while leaving the actual dark crack traces as unpainted corridors. Measured on the 620x618 panel, red = 22.3% of frame (85.4k px) with 89% of it in just two blobs (rows 141-345 x cols 89-584, and rows 325-561 x cols 36-584). The strongest thin dark-line pixels (top-2% black-tophat) are enriched inside red by only 1.94x over chance, 57% of them lie OUTSIDE red, and only 3.9% of red pixels are dark-line; meanwhile local std inside red is 29.8 vs 19.0 outside - i.e. the model is segmenting "textured/deformed zone", not "crack". Concretely: the single most convincing crack in panel 2, a long sharp dark line running left from the wedge tip at ~(row 300, col 560) through (row 330, col 470) to (row 355, col 405), is a clean unpainted hole straight through the middle of the red; and in the lower band the sharp black/white striated crack zone at rows ~415-450, cols 40-300 is largely unpainted while the smooth mottled material 30-60 px BELOW it is solidly red. True positives exist (the lens-shaped opening at rows 72-100, cols 358-410 is correctly covered) but the faint hairline continuing from its right tip diagonally down to ~(470,150) is missed. Wedge suppression is working - the large dark wedge at cols ~582-620, rows ~285-320 is excluded and its rim is not traced - but it is implemented as an abrupt rectangular cut (straight mask boundary at col 582, plus 20-26 px straight rectilinear boundary runs elsewhere), which also chops legitimate structure. Minor extra FPs on round ring/crescent artifact clusters (rows 178-216 x cols 227-273; rows 499-519 x cols 550-576). No off-specimen field or specimen edge exists in this crop, so neither contributes.

Gross dilation: the prediction is a solid blanket over the two broad deformation-relief / surface-topography bands rather than a trace of the crack itself. Red covers 29.5% of the frame, but only 13% of red pixels are actual dark line pixels and 24% of red sits on texture blander than the global median gradient, so per-pixel precision is roughly 0.2 and the real hairline crack (the thin branching dark trace running from the wedge mouth at ~(614,272) down-left through (430,310) to ~(250,380), plus the thin trace along the top margin of the lower band) is buried inside a mass of ~8x-too-large area. Two secondary problems compound it: (1) the wedge suppression is a crude axis-aligned rectangular hole punched only over the wedge's black core, so red still wraps the wedge rim, its bright/dark phase fringes, and its whole tapering tail, and runs up to a hard vertical wall at x=581; (2) the mask is hard-clipped by a ~34 px rectangular border exclusion (column counts jump 0 to 122 at x=34 and 175 to 0 at x=581), which means the classifier is still firing on the edge/boundary strip and is only being masked out by a geometric rule, not by having learned it. A smaller residual: the isolated vertical blob chains at x~500 and x~575-600 in the lower right follow straight seam/edge lines, not cracks. Positive notes: the regularly scattered ring/crescent reference artifacts in the top right are correctly left unpainted, and the real crack is not missed.

findings.dominant_fp_kind: dark wedge or notch (not a crack)
findings.biggest_remaining_problem: The suppression is inverted in effect: it punches holes out of the dark wedge/band CORES (only 37% of the strong dark features are red, and there is a clean rectangular hole over the darkest part of the lower band at panel x~250-375, y~475-560) while red blankets everything AROUND the wedge - 76% of the red sits within 25 px of the wedge/band complex and 65% of it is >12 px from any real feature, i.e. a 15-90 px thick halo over plain mottled matrix. The result is one 87k-px blob covering 26% of the frame with median width ~16 px, which is topologically nothing like a crack (real cracks here are a few px wide). It also shows hard rectilinear patch edges on the right (straight boundary at x~590 plus rectangular corners), so part of the decision is tile-quantised rather than feature-driven. Net effect: the one clearly real thin crack in the frame - the ~2-3 px dark/bright-paired near-vertical hairline at x~305-312 running y~352 to y~435 and bridging the upper band to the lower band - is captured only incidentally, in two disconnected blobs with a ~20 px gap at y~366-386 and no coverage below y~425, so it would not survive as a connected trace. Secondary FPs: small isolated red spots sitting on round pore/inclusion rings and dash-shaped inclusions in the upper half (e.g. y140-162/x266-289, y194-223/x244-282, y303-336/x460-509) and a blob over a mottled texture patch at bottom right.

No thinness/filament prior at all: 27% of the frame is a SINGLE 103,648-px amoeba that blankets the whole deformed/mottled zone including plainly featureless matrix (71% red at y300-340, x380-470) instead of tracing lines. It is also anti-correlated with the real linear evidence - the mask punches a hole along the darkest linear core of the lower band (only 35% red at y450-470, x60-200) while filling both flanks, and it paints the dark wedge tip 90.5% red (x95-175, y243-264) plus 42% of the right-edge dark rim (y180-198), so the wedge suppression is only cosmetic. The one genuine feature - 3-4 faint parallel hairlines at x293-312, y350-437 bridging the upper band into the lower one - is caught only ~50%, and only as incidental blob overspill. Straight axis-aligned mask clips (dead-straight edge at x=581, boundary runs of 23-31 px) additionally point to tile/patch-boundary artifacts in post-processing.

The prediction is a coarse region fill, not a thin-structure trace, and it is mislocalised relative to the damage it is supposed to follow. Red covers 25.0% of the frame in 48 components (90% of the area in just 5 blobs), yet only ~2.6% of the frame is red-on-actual-structure: 77% of red pixels lie more than 6 px from any high-contrast structure core, and 56% lie more than 15 px away. Worst case is the lower damage band (panel x 60-400, y 410-500): overlaying the darkest pixels shows red forms a HALO around it - the smooth matrix above and below the band is solid red while the band's own dark core and bright striated flanks are left completely unmarked (red fraction inside the two largest dark cores at x[142,230] y[449,475] and x[297,365] y[436,459] is 0.00). Same inversion logic elsewhere: the big right-hand blob (x 400-600, y 140-330) fills the featureless mottled interior of a raised lobe, and the centre blob (x 120-400, y 200-340) traces a lobe outline rather than a crack. Secondary signature: several red boundaries are axis-aligned and clipped to mosaic tile seams - a straight vertical cut at x approx 585, a rectangular patch at x 440-585 / y 345-400, and a straight horizontal cut at y approx 400 and at the bottom-right blob - so tile-level intensity offsets are still driving part of the mask. The genuinely thin crack in the frame (a few-pixel-wide vertical filament at x approx 297, y 358-403, hanging down from the upper band into the material near frame centre, clear in panel 2 and faintly in panel 1) is only about half covered: red touches its top junction, drops out over the middle ~40%, then a small isolated blob picks up the lower half and the dark tip. Good news: the wedge suppression is working - the dark tongue entering the right edge (x 563-619, y 302-331) has zero red inside it and zero within a 12 px rim, so the rim is no longer traced. The risk is that the same darkness-based suppression is now also deleting the dark cores of real cracks, which is exactly the halo pattern seen on the lower band.

The edge suppression is a fixed-width exclusion band (~8-14 px) but the local-contrast ringing from the hard bright->black step extends ~20 px, so the model now fires in a halo RING just OUTSIDE the exclusion zone instead of on the rim itself. Measured: 100% of the 1055 red pixels lie 8.2-20.0 px from a zero-valued (black) region (median 15 px; left cluster min 14 px, right cluster min 8 px), while only 9% of the bright field is within 22 px of black, and not one red pixel sits in the interior (>20 px from any edge). The suppression displaced the false positives rather than removing them; it needs to be distance-graded/widened to the full ringing radius, or keyed to "step edge present within N px" rather than "on the edge".

Two coupled problems, both about WHERE the red sits rather than whether cracks were found. (1) Edge/seam artifact family, ~16% of red area. A ragged vertical red column sits at x~18-30 running y~150-440, immediately inboard of the dead black frame column at x~5-10; panel 2 shows nothing crack-like there, and it runs perpendicular to every real crack in the frame, so it is a pure frame/mosaic-seam false positive (6.6% of red, ~6 components). On the right, 18% of red lies within 18px of the specimen boundary at x>470, and roughly half of that is spill onto the bright/dark boundary halo and onto the dark flank of the edge step/notch at x~480-515, y~200-235 rather than onto crack. The rim suppression is largely working - only 1.0% of red is within 3px of the boundary and 2.6% within 6px, so the classic thin-rim outline trace is gone - but red still bleeds up the notch flank as a diagonal arm, so the wedge/step is not fully suppressed. (2) Systematic blob fattening. Red regions are 2-4x wider than the actual few-pixel dark crack lines, and on branching cracks (the Y-branch at x399-486/y261-286, area 1195px, and the one at x203-258/y108-129) the red fills the solid triangle between the two arms instead of tracing them. 50% of red pixels sit on the top-5% local-contrast fringe and 90% are within 2px of one, so the dilation is only ~2px per side, but that is enough to destroy crack width, opening and branching morphology for any quantitative use. Recall is not the problem: a ridge/dark-line filter over panel 2 found 38 elongated interior features >=30px and every single one inside the specimen core is covered by red (coverage 0.85-1.00); the only uncovered dark lines are at x=5-9 (the frame bar) and a 42x4 vertical line at x=509 (boundary rim), both correctly left alone. Real cracks are unambiguously present and correctly identified: sharp, thin, dark, phase-fringed, branching, all oriented near-horizontal (consistent with a vertical tensile axis), including a genuine crack emanating leftward from the notch root at y~218 and a faint hairline at x525-555/y~29 that only shows in panel 2 and is marked. Fix priority: mask the left frame/dead-column strip and widen the boundary-halo exclusion by ~10px on the right, then reduce the morphological closing/dilation so branch arms stay separate.

The detector is locked onto a per-tile repeating fixed-pattern artifact, not onto cracks. Measured directly on the red mask: shifting it by 112 px in x gives IoU 0.23 and by 110 px in y gives IoU 0.16, while half-period shifts (56 px, 55 px) give 0.05 and 0.02 - so the predictions are periodic at exactly the mosaic tile pitch. Side-by-side high-pass patches at x = 48, 160, 272, 384 (same y) show the IDENTICAL motif (a fan of parallel diagonal hatch strokes plus a ring/crescent) replicated at each lattice node. Every feature I chased as a possible hairline turned out to be one of these clones: the "branching hook" at panel-2 (180, 485), the convincing-looking faint diagonal that appears to run inward from the notch at (419, 261) -> (358, 294), and the streak at (150, 420). All are lattice members, so there is no crack in this frame and ~all 23,385 red pixels / 260 regions are false positive. Morphology confirms the model is a dark-blob detector rather than a curvilinear detector: 84% of regions have aspect ratio < 2, only 2% exceed 4, median region size 34 px, and no red or image structure anywhere forms a connected elongated path (longest dark ridge found by a multi-scale Sato filter in the specimen interior is ~40 px, and it is a lattice clone). Secondary problems: (a) the wedge/edge rim suppression is only partial - 18% of red area lies within 40 px of the right specimen/wedge boundary and an elongated strip hugs the rim contour for a 42-row continuous run at rows 16-58 plus 23-25 row runs at 548-571 and 576-601, i.e. 28% of all image rows have red within 22 px inside that boundary; (b) a solid vertical red line at x = 16-25 spanning 77% of image height tracks the left frame/tile edge (19% of red area); (c) 34% of interior red sits in the 14% of rows nearest the tile seam rows 115/226/332/441/551, a 2.4x enrichment. Net effect: the false-positive noise floor (6.4% of frame) is dense enough at the exact scale of a real microcrack that a genuine faint hairline could not be distinguished from it, so this output is not usable as-is. Fix priority: suppress tile-periodic fixed-pattern features (median across tiles, or a per-tile-phase feature the classifier can reject), add an elongation/curvilinearity gate before the final dilation, and extend the rim suppression to the frame border and to the top/bottom corners where the boundary meets the frame.

The prediction is an area fill, not a crack trace. Red is 23.4% of the frame but 89% of it sits in only 2 amorphous blobs (44,182 px at x92-590/y147-358 and 35,503 px at x42-590/y311-535), whereas a multiscale dark-ridge (valley) detector finds only ~3.2% of the frame (12,215 px) of genuine thin elongated filaments. Allowing a generous +/-3-5 px tolerance around every filament still leaves 70-79% of red unexplained; ~1/3 of red pixels (27% even after 6 px erosion of the mask core) lie on matrix whose local 7x7 std is below the frame's 60th percentile, i.e. visibly featureless. Consequences: (1) the mask engulfs the rough deformation-band texture and the smooth matrix flanking it instead of the few-pixel dark lines inside it; (2) the wedge is not suppressed - the sharp dark wedge tip near x100-235/y245-280 is solid red including its rim, and along the large bright wedge at x420-590/y255-320 the red boundary hugs the wedge's upper dark rim and fills everything above it, with axis-aligned rectangular blocks over the lower rim; (3) suppression appears inverted in places - a clean axis-aligned rectangular hole (~x117-237, y430-472) has been carved out of the lower blob exactly over the crispest continuous dark crack line in the lower band, while the surrounding matrix stays painted; (4) despite the 7x area inflation recall on the filaments is only 54%, and the entire branching thin-line network at x420-590/y505-570 (bottom right, ridge fraction 0.073/0.037 in those grid cells) is completely unpainted. There is also clear tile/patch blockiness: a 103-px perfectly straight vertical mask edge at x=589 plus several 23-28 px straight edges at rows 303/336/365/417/434/470 and cols 41/116/454.

The edge/rim suppression is not working on either boundary, and there is no crack in this frame for the model to have found, so the output is essentially all noise. Quantitatively: 43.3% of the red is four long vertical strips at x=12-21 pinned ~10 px inside the black field-of-view border at x=0-2 (also the x=19 mosaic seam) on completely featureless bright material; another 30.2% is a broken chain of 16 blobs hugging the right specimen/dark-notch boundary, sitting squarely on the bright rim and its dark transition band (largest single blob, 234 px at x=491-505, y=76-108, is entirely on that rim); the remaining 26.5% is 33 tiny blobs dropped onto individual short bipolar surface-relief arcs in the interior. Multi-scale ridge filtering of panel 2 inside the eroded specimen returns nothing with skeleton length above 30 px, and the one sinuous hairline candidate (x=385-445, y=28-48) resolves at 14x into the same dark-plus-bright relief signature as the ~100 uniformly distributed, commonly oriented texture arcs elsewhere. Priority fix is a hard geometric veto: reject any pixel within ~25 px of the specimen mask boundary or of the frame/mosaic-seam lines (grid period ~81 px, seams at x=19+81k, y=60+81k), then require a minimum skeleton length and monopolar (purely dark) profile before emitting anything, which would zero out this frame as it should.

Two thirds of the red (2600 of 3931 px, ~44 blobs) sits on the ubiquitous population of discrete LENS/CIGAR-shaped objects with a dark core flanked by bright bands (elongated inclusions or relief scratches, ~20-40 px long x 8-16 px wide, aspect only 2-5:1, blunt rounded ends, isolated and scattered uniformly over the whole field, including far from centre). Dozens of visually identical objects are left unmarked, so the classifier is effectively scoring "locally high-contrast elongated blob", not "thin connected line". Because these FPs are elongated, a circularity/round-pore filter will not remove them - the discriminator that works here is WIDTH and CONNECTED LENGTH: the one true crack is 1-2 px wide with a 100 px continuous ridge (aspect ~27:1, ridge-elongation 27 in a Hessian test), while every FP has aspect <8 and ridge length <40 px. A min-length/max-width (or eigenvalue-ratio) gate on the connected component would delete ~85% of the red while keeping the crack intact.

The output behaves as a generic low-contrast-texture threshold rather than a crack detector: 20% of the frame is red across 313 blobs, but only ~10% of that red is anywhere near the one real hairline (x 105-345, y 160-210), while ~36% is scattered mottling/ring-artifact blobs in featureless bulk, ~33% is thick bands hugging the dark wedge rim (the suppression stopped interior infill but not rim tracing), and ~22% is a hard convolution/padding halo along the top and left frame edges (rows and columns 12-30 are 45-80% red). Even where the crack is covered, it is swallowed by a ~40-px-wide blob, so no usable crack width, length, or branching geometry can be recovered from this mask.

The dark-feature suppression has inverted the prediction at the one place that matters: it punches a hard, tile-aligned red-free hole straight through the strongest real crack (panel-2/3 coords x=191-400, y=294-369 - only 28% of that dark crack core is red), while the model blankets the surrounding bland matrix with 31% red. The wedge rim itself is no longer traced (a rectangular suppression box cleanly excludes both the right-edge notch at x=573-620, y=204-228 and its bright rim), so the suppression fixed the rim artifact but is now over-firing onto genuine wide/open crack. Combined with a blob-shaped classifier output (one 69.5k-px component = 80% of all red, only 24% of red lies within 4 px of any dark linear feature, vs a plausible true crack area of ~4-6% of frame), the result is a damage-zone blob detector rather than a crack tracer: it neither delineates the thin faint branches (e.g. the sharp hairline at x~368 running y=310 up to a clear T-junction at y~250, and the thin lines trailing left from the notch tip at y~195-215) nor stays off texture, calibration crescents (x~490-560/y~240-300, x~500-570/y~420-490), elongated pores (x~170-200/y~130-165), and the frame border strips.

The output is a texture/contrast blanket, not a crack tracing: 39.3% of the frame in 109 amorphous blobs whose boundaries bear no relation to any linear feature. Measured against a strict thin-dark-line (Hessian valley) filter set to the top 3% of ridge response, only 21% of red pixels lie within 2 px of any line-like structure, and red covers just 57% of that line content -- barely above the 39% a random mask of the same area would achieve. So the model is not even buying recall with its enormous area; it is filling whichever mosaic tiles have grainier texture (red masses in the upper-left, mid-left and upper-right sit on plain mottling with no linear feature at all, and the mask terminates along perfectly straight vertical/horizontal tile seams at panel x~33, x~600 and several horizontal cuts). Meanwhile genuine thin features are dropped: a long sharp dark line at roughly panel coords x 240-300, y 175-195 falls just outside a red blob whose interior is featureless texture. On the wedge: the suppression does carve holes over the dark cores (the lower-centre blocky wedge near x 250-400, y 285-320 and the right-edge notch near x 555-625, y 185-215 are left grey), but the carve-outs are straight-edged bounding cuts and red still hugs both silhouettes pixel-tight, covers their bright halos and the dark streak extensions running left and right of the notch tip -- so the rim is still effectively being delineated, just as the boundary of a bulk region rather than a thin trace. Fix priority: enforce elongation/width and skeleton-continuity constraints on candidate regions and drop area-dominant blobs before any further threshold tuning; a 39% mask cannot be salvaged by suppressing individual artifacts.

The prediction is region-level, not crack-level: 82% of all red is ONE amorphous component covering 27% of the frame (bbox y80-420, x123-594, solidity 0.59), and only 25% of red pixels sit within 2 px of a strong ridge (44% within 4 px), so ~70% of the red is dilated deformation-zone mottling / microstructure texture around the cracks rather than the cracks themselves. Worse, the suppression inverts locally: the two most crack-like features are punched OUT as holes while the surrounding matrix is painted - (a) the elongated tapering crack running left from the notch tip (approx x440-580, y185-215) is left unpainted as a white carve-out, and (b) the open central crack / dark lens (approx x255-350, y280-315) sits in a blocky rectangular carve-out with red packed hard against every side. Net effect: nothing crack-shaped is delineated - a real branching crack network IS clearly present in panel 2 (best seen at x120-340/y240-380 and x20-180/y110-260) and ~72% of the strongest ridge pixels fall inside red, but only incidentally, because the blob swallows the entire damage band. Secondary FPs: isolated blobs on quiet upper-frame matrix / faint mottling (x175-260/y70-155, x395-465/y27-50) and one blob abutting a scattered ring-crescent reference artifact near x290/y75. Encouraging: red never lands on off-specimen black, only 1.3% of red is on lowest-quartile flat matrix, no mosaic-seam or specimen-edge tracing, and the wedge/notch rim is clean - red stops at a hard vertical cut at x~592 and never reaches the dark wedge, so that suppression works.

The prediction is inverted at the feature level: the dark-feature suppression that was added for the wedge is not wedge-specific, so it also vetoes the genuine crack, while the classifier floods the featureless matrix. Measured: red covers 43.1% of the frame, but the central dark crack core (connected dark component at y280-302, x239-321, clearly a branching crack in panel 2) is only 0.4% red, and its 1-8 px rim only 3-10% red — i.e. the one unambiguous crack in the image is punched OUT of the mask while the smooth matrix around it is painted in. Only 24.6% of red pixels sit on any local structure at all (|p1 - median15| > 18), and only 6.7% sit on an elongated linear feature; ~75% of red is on flat mottled matrix. The mask also has a hard rectangular envelope (red switches on abruptly at x=32, off at x=600, on at y=26) with its densest columns (65-71% red) hugging the left specimen-edge/valid-region boundary, so a valid-region/edge-rim artifact is being learned as crack. Net effect: the suppression fixed the wedge rim (1-8 px band around the wedge is 1-4% red vs 43% globally, well below chance, and the wedge interior is 0.0% red) but at the cost of deleting the true positive, and the underlying pixel classifier has essentially no crack specificity — it is thresholding low-frequency shading, not linear structure. Fix direction: make the dark/wedge veto shape-aware (reject only large low-elongation saturated-dark blobs contiguous with the frame edge, not thin elongated dark ridges), and add an elongation/ridge-response gate to the positive class so 42% of a frame cannot be labelled crack.

One contiguous 1664-px blob (51% of ALL red, ~74% of all false positive area) in the bright granular/mottled thin corner just inside the specimen edge and below the notch (panel coords x 40-87, y 194-274; ~7-14% of width, 67-95% of height). It is fat and amoeba-shaped with no elongated structure in panel 2 at that location - pure microstructure/mottling plus round pores in a thinned notch-flank region. Fixing this one region would cut total false positive area by three quarters. Close second: the red on the genuine crack stops dead at x=341, so the entire upper-right branch of the crack (panel 2, x 343-425, y 75-115) is missed, and the covered part is broken into 4 disjoint segments instead of one connected trace. Third: the wedge suppression only converted the rim trace from a solid line into a dotted arc (~18 small components, ~17% of red) that still follows the notch boundary from y=12 to y=220.

All four red regions (206 px total, 0.053% of the 625x625 frame) sit directly on the specimen outline's phase-contrast fringe, not inside the material: red at y22-34/x497-504, y134-151/x451-460, y254-263/x426-428, y366-385/x425-428 versus a measured specimen-to-empty-field boundary at x=504 (y=28), 459 (y=140), 430 (y=258), 427 (y=375) - i.e. every blob is within 0-4 px of the bright/dark edge fringe. Notably, three of the four coincide with abrupt lateral STEP discontinuities in the outline (measured edge jumps at y=144, 265, 479), which are mosaic-tile stitching misregistrations that locally double/kink the edge fringe; the model fires exactly there. So the existing wedge/rim suppression is not covering the specimen-boundary fringe when tile seams jog it. There is no dark wedge/notch in this frame at all - the dark area is the uniform off-specimen field (value 0 out to the right frame border, containing two regularly spaced small calibration rings at x~590, y~190 and y~410), so the wedge suppression is untested here rather than failing. Interior verdict: panel 2 (and 4x/5x local-contrast and Sato ridge maps of the interior with a 14 px edge erosion) shows only dust/inclusion clusters, small round pores and mottling - the largest dark ridge component is a 43x11 px blob at x161-204, y115-126 with no elongated connected structure anywhere. The only linear features are pin-thin, perfectly straight lines that fan symmetrically up-left and down-left from the edge jog points and terminate at the boundary; their straightness, symmetry and origin at tile corners mark them as stitching/streak artifacts, not cracks. I do not see a real crack in this frame, so this is a precision leak on a near-empty frame rather than a miss - net effect is small in area but the model's entire positive class here is wrong. Recommended fix: extend the rim suppression to the full specimen/field boundary transition (dilate the outline mask by ~8-12 px and reject candidates whose orientation is parallel to the local boundary), which would zero this frame out.

The wedge/boundary suppression is still failing: a long, continuous, boundary-parallel red band runs just inside the bright rim of the left dark notch/wedge (largest non-crack component, ~1700 px, spanning roughly y=14-125 at x=103-158 in panel coordinates, plus more of the same at y=209-272 and y=291-321), and it is joined by a "picture-frame" of speckle clutter hugging the top and bottom periphery. Quantitatively, of the 13,292 red pixels (6.3% of the frame, 139 connected components): ~19% sit in the left rim/notch band, ~16% in a top peripheral band (y<45), ~19% in a bottom peripheral band (y>285), and ~5% in off-specimen/right-edge/interior specks - i.e. ~60% of the red is plainly off-target, on featureless material or pure edge/vignette transition where panel 2 shows nothing linear. Only one red component (41.7% of red, y=121-207, x=128-367) is on the genuine feature, and even there it is over-dilated roughly 4-5x the true hairline width (crack is 2-4 px; red streak is 10-20 px), so any crack-width, area, or region-count metric derived from this mask will be badly biased. The good news: the real crack is unambiguous in panel 2 - a branching hairline network emanating from the notch at mid-height, fanning into up/down branches near the mouth and consolidating into a single trunk that runs right to about x=370, and the red covers that trunk end-to-end with its tip terminating within a few pixels of where the crack fades out. This crack receives ZERO red -- red's max x is 563, the crack starts at 564, so overlap is exactly nil. Net behaviour is the worst combination: false positives concentrated on the one artifact the owner explicitly excluded, plus a 0% hit rate on the actual crack. Fix direction: make the wedge suppression a dilated exclusion zone around the whole notch halo rather than just the rim ridge, and restore sensitivity to low-amplitude high-aspect-ratio ridge features away from the notch, since the missed crack is faint but geometrically unambiguous.

findings.dominant_fp_kind: dark wedge or notch (not a crack)
findings.biggest_remaining_problem: The wedge suppression did not remove the rim trace, it only displaced and fragmented it: measured on the panel-3 red mask, 0 of 1243 red pixels lie within 2 px of the dark void, but 82% lie within 10 px and 96% within 20 px of it (median offset 7.2 px), and 73% of red sits at x>=360 where the void is a wide notch, forming a dashed halo (29 components) that follows the upper and lower notch outline point-for-point through the deformation-texture band. Meanwhile the one genuinely crack-like feature - the thin 1-13 px slit that tapers left out of the notch from x~375 to a tip at x~288, plus the mottled process zone ahead of it - receives only ~16-27% of the red, concentrated as a collar around the tip and a couple of dabs at the x~353-361 kink; its centreline is never traced (only 41% of its columns have red within +/-8 px, and no red pixel lies on the slit itself). Net effect: the model spends most of its output re-drawing the notch boundary at a fixed standoff and under-traces the actual crack, so the suppression needs to be widened to the whole notch neighbourhood (or made thickness-aware, keeping only voids thinner than ~15 px) and paired with a term that rewards tracing along the thin slit's length rather than around it.

The prediction is a material-vs-air segmentation, not crack detection: red is one solid blob filling the whole specimen body (25.2% of frame = 72.8% of the specimen area; the 2 largest components hold ~96% of the red), driven by the dense round-pore / mottled microstructure that lights up under local-contrast enhancement. Measured share of red by zone: 80.7% on-specimen bulk texture (98% of every interior pixel painted), 14.1% specimen edge/boundary rim band, 4.6% wedge-rim band, 0.7% off-specimen reference-artifact specks (~82 tiny components). There is no elongation/linearity or thinness constraint anywhere in the decision: the model rewards "textured metal" instead of "thin connected dark line", so a blanket-fill on a crack-free frame scores as 108 detections. The wedge-interior suppression works (density 0.002 inside the dark notch, clean ~8-10 px white buffer), but red immediately re-forms a contour parallel to the notch top/bottom rims and a dense wreath around the notch tip, so the wedge outline is still effectively delineated at a small offset. Fix priority: gate on ridge/tubularity (thin dark line response with high aspect ratio and connectivity) and hard-reject blobs whose area/skeleton-length ratio exceeds a few pixels, plus widen the wedge/edge exclusion band beyond the current ~8 px.

The wedge/edge suppression only DISPLACED the rim tracing instead of removing it. Measured against the panel-1 background mask, ZERO red pixels lie within 3 px of the wedge/boundary and only 1% within 5 px, but 33% sit at 5-8 px and 66% within 12 px - a dashed "standoff outline" that hugs the notch rim and the specimen right edge at a fixed ~6-12 px offset, riding the bright/dark ringing halo that the local-contrast enhancement creates alongside every high-contrast boundary (clearly visible as the double dark/bright line in panel 2 at e.g. x~525-540, y~165-195). So the suppression band needs to be wider AND the classifier needs a feature that rejects the LCE ringing halo itself, not just the black pixels. Secondary problem: the one genuine feature is fused into the same connected component as the rim trace, so it cannot be recovered by any downstream size/shape filter.

The dark-region/boundary-rim suppression is not working on this frame: ~90% of all red is a thick blobby band welded to the specimen edge (31% within 25 px of the boundary, 33% at 25-60 px, plus a 3400-px solid slab filling the top-left corner that reaches 60-90 px into completely featureless material). It has just been displaced from the black side of the rim onto the bright/grey transition shoulder on the specimen side, so it reads as "inside the material" to any distance-to-edge heuristic while still being pure edge artifact. The remaining ~10% is the regular ~95 px lattice of reference/calibration marks along the top row (6.5%) and the right frame column (3.4%). Meanwhile the interior contains zero crack: >60 px from the edge there are only six specks of 5-9 px (0.3% of red), and multi-scale ridge/matched-filter searches over the interior return nothing but the periodic mosaic pattern (horizontal seams every ~95 px, 45-degree diagonals, curl/crescent motifs on a regular grid) plus grain mottling. So on a crack-free frame the model still paints 3.1% of the field across 110 regions - i.e. this frame contributes essentially only false-positive area, and the 110-region count is dominated by the artifact lattice being fragmented into dozens of tiny detections.

all_results.biggest_remaining_problem: The model is not segmenting cracks at all - it is segmenting "high local texture variance," and the wedge suppression is now a hard axis-aligned box that deletes the single best crack in the frame. Quantitatively: red = 28.6% of the frame and 80% of that mass is ONE connected amorphous blob (63,422 of 78,900 px, ~23% of frame). Mean panel-1 intensity inside red (136.6) is indistinguishable from outside (140.3), while local std inside red is ~2x outside (30.6 vs 16.0) - proof the classifier keys on deformation mottling / relief texture, not on dark thin linear voids. The mask boundary meanders through texture and never traces a line; it is blobby, isotropic, and 19% of it sits on genuinely bland matrix (local sd below the frame median). Simultaneously the suppression over-fires: the four largest near-black elongated features - x277-377/y306-325 (the 100-px central dark crack trace), x383-437/y301-320, x594-619/y206-224, x541-592/y220-232 - have EXACTLY 0.000 red coverage. A straight vertical mask edge at column 598 spanning 147 rows, plus straight horizontal edges around the central dark trace, confirms rectangular box suppression rather than a learned decision. The most unambiguous crack in the image is at native x~500-620, y~190-250: a classic open crack with a dark void core and bright phase-contrast fringes, propagating LEFT from the mid-dark uniform wedge/notch that intrudes at the right frame edge, tapering to a crack tip, with 2-3 converging branches. That is textbook crack-from-notch-tip and it sits in a clean rectangular hole in the mask surrounded by a sea of red on featureless matrix. So the wedge rim itself is no longer being traced (suppression works on the wedge), but the box swallowed the crack emanating from the wedge tip - the exact structure the specimen owner cares about. Only incidental fragments of the crack network get red (x467-500/y203-221, x537-585/y193-201, x423-462/y350-362, x245-271/y307-316 are covered, but only because the giant blob happens to sweep over them, not because they were traced). Net effect: precision and recall fail at the same time, and the suppression is now actively harmful. Fix direction: replace area-thresholded texture/variance response with an anisotropy-gated ridge/valley detector (require elongation and dark-core polarity), and replace the rectangular wedge box with a tight morphological mask of the wedge body only, dilated by a few px, so cracks emanating from the notch tip survive.

The mask is anti-localised with respect to the cracks: it blanket-fills the deformed high-relief material AROUND the damage while leaving the actual dark crack traces as unpainted corridors. Measured on the 620x618 panel, red = 22.3% of frame (85.4k px) with 89% of it in just two blobs (rows 141-345 x cols 89-584, and rows 325-561 x cols 36-584). Gross dilation: the prediction is a solid blanket over the two broad deformation-relief / surface-topography bands rather than a trace of the crack itself. Red covers 29.5% of the frame, but only 13% of red pixels are actual dark line pixels and 24% of red sits on texture blander than the global median gradient, so per-pixel precision is roughly 0.2 and the real hairline crack (the thin branching dark trace running from the wedge mouth at ~(614,272) down-left through (430,310) to ~(250,380), plus the thin trace along the top margin of the lower band) is buried inside a mass of ~8x-too-large area. Two secondary problems compound it: (1) the wedge suppression is a crude axis-aligned rectangular hole punched only over the wedge's black core, so red still wraps the wedge rim, its bright/dark phase fringes, and its whole tapering tail, and runs up to a hard vertical wall at x=581; (2) the mask is hard-clipped by a ~34 px rectangular border exclusion (column counts jump 0 to 122 at x=34 and 175 to 0 at x=581), which means the classifier is still firing on the edge/boundary strip and is only being masked out by a geometric rule, not by having learned it. all_results.dominant_fp_kind: dark wedge or notch (not a crack)

The edge suppression is a fixed-width exclusion band (~8-14 px) but the local-contrast ringing from the hard bright->black step extends ~20 px, so the model now fires in a halo RING just OUTSIDE the exclusion zone instead of on the rim itself. Measured: 100% of the 1055 red pixels lie 8.2-20.0 px from a zero-valued (black) region (median 15 px; left cluster min 14 px, right cluster min 8 px), while only 9% of the bright field is within 22 px of black, and not one red pixel sits in the interior (>20 px from any edge). The suppression displaced the false positives rather than removing them; it needs to be distance-graded/widened to the full ringing radius, or keyed to "step edge present within N px" rather than "on the edge".

Two coupled problems, both about WHERE the red sits rather than whether cracks were found. (1) Edge/seam artifact family, ~16% of red area. A ragged vertical red column sits at x~18-30 running y~150-440, immediately inboard of the dead black frame column at x~5-10; panel 2 shows nothing crack-like there, and it runs perpendicular to every real crack in the frame, so it is a pure frame/mosaic-seam false positive (6.6% of red, ~6 components). On the right, 18% of red lies within 18px of the specimen boundary at x>470, and roughly half of that is spill onto the bright/dark boundary halo and onto the dark flank of the edge step/notch at x~480-515, y~200-235 rather than onto crack. The rim suppression is largely working - only 1.0% of red is within 3px of the boundary and 2.6% within 6px, so the classic thin-rim outline trace is gone - but red still bleeds up the notch flank as a diagonal arm, so the wedge/step is not fully suppressed. (2) Systematic blob fattening. Recall is not the problem: a ridge/dark-line filter over panel 2 found 38 elongated interior features >=30px and every single one inside the specimen core is covered by red (coverage 0.85-1.00); the only uncovered dark lines are at x=5-9 (the frame bar) and a 42x4 vertical line at x=509 (boundary rim), both correctly left alone. The detector is locked onto a per-tile repeating fixed-pattern artifact, not onto cracks. Measured directly on the red mask: shifting it by 112 px in x gives IoU 0.23 and by 110 px in y gives IoU 0.16, while half-period shifts (56 px, 55 px) give 0.05 and 0.02 - so the predictions are periodic at exactly the mosaic tile pitch. Side-by-side high-pass patches at x = 48, 160, 272, 384 (same y) show the IDENTICAL motif (a fan of parallel diagonal hatch strokes plus a ring/crescent) replicated at each lattice node. Every feature I chased as a possible hairline turned out to be one of these clones: the "branching hook" at panel-2 (180, 485), the convincing-looking faint diagonal that appears to run inward from the notch at (419, 261) -> (358, 294), and the streak at (150, 420). All are lattice members, so there is no crack in this frame and ~all 23,385 red pixels / 260 regions are false positive. Morphology confirms the model is a dark-blob detector rather than a curvilinear detector: 84% of regions have aspect ratio < 2, only 2% exceed 4, median region size 34 px, and no red or image structure anywhere forms a connected elongated path (longest dark ridge found by a multi-scale Sato filter in the specimen interior is ~40 px, and it is a lattice clone). Secondary problems: (a) the wedge/edge rim suppression is only partial - 18% of red area lies within 40 px of the right specimen/wedge boundary and an elongated strip hugs the rim contour for a 42-row continuous run at rows 16-58 plus 23-25 row runs at 548-571 and 576-601, i.e. 28% of all image rows have red within 22 px inside that boundary; (b) a solid vertical red line at x = 16-25 spanning 77% of image height tracks the left frame/tile edge (19% of red area); (c) 34% of interior red sits in the 14% of rows nearest the tile seam rows 115/226/332/441/551, a 2.4x enrichment. Net effect: the false-positive noise floor (6.4% of frame) is dense enough at the exact scale of a real microcrack that a genuine faint hairline could not be distinguished from it, so this output is not usable as-is. Fix priority: suppress tile-periodic fixed-pattern features (median across tiles, or a per-tile-phase feature the classifier can reject), add an elongation/curvilinearity gate before the final dilation, and extend the rim suppression to the frame border and to the top/bottom corners where the boundary meets the frame.

The prediction is an area fill, not a crack trace. Red is 23.4% of the frame but 89% of it sits in only 2 amorphous blobs (44,182 px at x92-590/y147-358 and 35,503 px at x42-590/y311-535), whereas a multiscale dark-ridge (valley) detector finds only ~3.2% of the frame (12,215 px) of genuine thin elongated filaments. Allowing a generous +/-3-5 px tolerance around every filament still leaves 70-79% of red unexplained; ~1/3 of red pixels (27% even after 6 px erosion of the mask core) lie on matrix whose local 7x7 std is below the frame's 60th percentile, i.e. visibly featureless. Consequences: (1) the mask engulfs the rough deformation-band texture and the smooth matrix flanking it instead of the few-pixel dark lines inside it; (2) the wedge is not suppressed - the sharp dark wedge tip near x100-235/y245-280 is solid red including its rim, and along the large bright wedge at x420-590/y255-320 the red boundary hugs the wedge's upper dark rim and fills everything above it, with axis-aligned rectangular blocks over the lower rim; (3) suppression appears inverted in places - a clean axis-aligned rectangular hole (~x117-237, y430-472) has been carved out of the lower blob exactly over the crispest continuous dark crack line in the lower band, while the surrounding matrix stays painted; (4) despite the 7x area inflation recall on the filaments is only 54%, and the entire branching thin-line network at x420-590/y505-570 (bottom right, ridge fraction 0.073/0.037 in those grid cells) is completely unpainted. There is also clear tile/patch blockiness: a 103-px perfectly straight vertical mask edge at x=589 plus several 23-28 px straight edges at rows 303/336/365/417/434/470 and cols 41/116/454.

The edge/rim suppression is not working on either boundary, and there is no crack in this frame for the model to have found, so the output is essentially all noise. Quantitatively: 43.3% of the red is four long vertical strips at x=12-21 pinned ~10 px inside the black field-of-view border at x=0-2 (also the x=19 mosaic seam) on completely featureless bright material; another 30.2% is a broken chain of 16 blobs hugging the right specimen/dark-notch boundary, sitting squarely on the bright rim and its dark transition band (largest single blob, 234 px at x=491-505, y=76-108, is entirely on that rim); the remaining 26.5% is 33 tiny blobs dropped onto individual short bipolar surface-relief arcs in the interior. Multi-scale ridge filtering of panel 2 inside the eroded specimen returns nothing with skeleton length above 30 px, and the one sinuous hairline candidate (x=385-445, y=28-48) resolves at 14x into the same dark-plus-bright relief signature as the ~100 uniformly distributed, commonly oriented texture arcs elsewhere. Priority fix is a hard geometric veto: reject any pixel within ~25 px of the specimen mask boundary or of the frame/mosaic-seam lines (grid period ~81 px, seams at x=19+81k, y=60+81k), then require a minimum skeleton length and monopolar (purely dark) profile before emitting anything, which would zero out this frame as it should.

Two thirds of the red (2600 of 3931 px, ~44 blobs) sits on the ubiquitous population of discrete LENS/CIGAR-shaped objects with a dark core flanked by bright bands (elongated inclusions or relief scratches, ~20-40 px long x 8-16 px wide, aspect only 2-5:1, blunt rounded ends, isolated and scattered uniformly over the whole field, including far from centre). Dozens of visually identical objects are left unmarked, so the classifier is effectively scoring "locally high-contrast elongated blob", not "thin connected line". Because these FPs are elongated, a circularity/round-pore filter will not remove them - the discriminator that works here is WIDTH and CONNECTED LENGTH: the one true crack is 1-2 px wide with a 100 px continuous ridge (aspect ~27:1, ridge-elongation 27 in a Hessian test), while every FP has aspect <8 and ridge length <40 px. A min-length/max-width (or eigenvalue-ratio) gate on the connected component would delete ~85% of the red while keeping the crack intact.

The output behaves as a generic low-contrast-texture threshold rather than a crack detector: 20% of the frame is red across 313 blobs, but only ~10% of that red is anywhere near the one real hairline (x 105-345, y 160-210), while ~36% is scattered mottling/ring-artifact blobs in featureless bulk, ~33% is thick bands hugging the dark wedge rim (the suppression stopped interior infill but not rim tracing), and ~22% is a hard convolution/padding halo along the top and left frame edges (rows and columns 12-30 are 45-80% red). Even where the crack is covered, it is swallowed by a ~40-px-wide blob, so no usable crack width, length, or branching geometry can be recovered from this mask.

The dark-feature suppression has inverted the prediction at the one place that matters: it punches a hard, tile-aligned red-free hole straight through the strongest real crack (panel-2/3 coords x=191-400, y=294-369 - only 28% of that dark crack core is red), while the model blankets the surrounding bland matrix with 31% red. The wedge rim itself is no longer traced (a rectangular suppression box cleanly excludes both the right-edge notch at x=573-620, y=204-228 and its bright rim), so the suppression fixed the rim artifact but is now over-firing onto genuine wide/open crack. Combined with a blob-shaped classifier output (one 69.5k-px component = 80% of all red, only 24% of red lies within 4 px of any dark linear feature, vs a plausible true crack area of ~4-6% of frame), the result is a damage-zone blob detector rather than a crack tracer: it neither delineates the thin faint branches (e.g. the sharp hairline at x~368 running y=310 up to a clear T-junction at y~250, and the thin lines trailing left from the notch tip at y~195-215) nor stays off texture, calibration crescents (x~490-560/y~240-300, x~500-570/y~420-490), elongated pores (x~170-200/y~130-165), and the frame border strips.

The output is a texture/contrast blanket, not a crack tracing: 39.3% of the frame in 109 amorphous blobs whose boundaries bear no relation to any linear feature. Measured against a strict thin-dark-line (Hessian valley) filter set to the top 3% of ridge response, only 21% of red pixels lie within 2 px of any line-like structure, and red covers just 57% of that line content -- barely above the 39% a random mask of the same area would achieve. So the model is not even buying recall with its enormous area; it is filling whichever mosaic tiles have grainier texture (red masses in the upper-left, mid-left and upper-right sit on plain mottling with no linear feature at all, and the mask terminates along perfectly straight vertical/horizontal tile seams at panel x~33, x~600 and several horizontal cuts). Meanwhile genuine thin features are dropped: a long sharp dark line at roughly panel coords x 240-300, y 175-195 falls just outside a red blob whose interior is featureless texture. On the wedge: the suppression does carve holes over the dark cores (the lower-centre blocky wedge near x 250-400, y 285-320 and the right-edge notch near x 555-625, y 185-215 are left grey), but the carve-outs are straight-edged bounding cuts and red still hugs both silhouettes pixel-tight, covers their bright halos and the dark streak extensions running left and right of the notch tip -- so the rim is still effectively being delineated, just as the boundary of a bulk region rather than a thin trace. Fix priority: enforce elongation/width and skeleton-continuity constraints on candidate regions and drop area-dominant blobs before any further threshold tuning; a 39% mask cannot be salvaged by suppressing individual artifacts.

The prediction is region-level, not crack-level: 82% of all red is ONE amorphous component covering 27% of the frame (bbox y80-420, x123-594, solidity 0.59), and only 25% of red pixels sit within 2 px of a strong ridge (44% within 4 px), so ~70% of the red is dilated deformation-zone mottling / microstructure texture around the cracks rather than the cracks themselves. Worse, the suppression inverts locally: the two most crack-like features are punched OUT as holes while the surrounding matrix is painted - (a) the elongated tapering crack running left from the notch tip (approx x440-580, y185-215) is left unpainted as a white carve-out, and (b) the open central crack / dark lens (approx x255-350, y280-315) sits in a blocky rectangular carve-out with red packed hard against every side. Net effect: nothing crack-shaped is delineated - a real branching crack network IS clearly present in panel 2 (best seen at x120-340/y240-380 and x20-180/y110-260) and ~72% of the strongest ridge pixels fall inside red, but only incidentally, because the blob swallows the entire damage band. Secondary FPs: isolated blobs on quiet upper-frame matrix / faint mottling (x175-260/y70-155, x395-465/y27-50) and one blob abutting a scattered ring-crescent reference artifact near x290/y75. Encouraging: red never lands on off-specimen black, only 1.3% of red is on lowest-quartile flat matrix, no mosaic-seam or specimen-edge tracing, and the wedge/notch rim is clean - red stops at a hard vertical cut at x~592 and never reaches the dark wedge, so that suppression works.

The prediction is inverted at the feature level: the dark-feature suppression that was added for the wedge is not wedge-specific, so it also vetoes the genuine crack, while the classifier floods the featureless matrix.
